incoming.name: Jimmy Wales
incoming.excerpt: In 2006, he joined the Board of Directors of the non-profit organization Creative Commons.

incoming.name: Open source
incoming.excerpt: The open-source concept has also been applied to media other than computer programs, e.g., by Creative Commons.

incoming.name: Wikinews
incoming.excerpt: Unlike Wikimedia's other projects, Wikinews contents are mostly available under Creative Commons Attribution 2.5 or later.

incoming.name: Wikipedia
incoming.excerpt: There is also content released under different copyleft terms or licenses that are compatible with the GFDL, such as images under Creative Commons licenses.

outgoing.name: Information
outgoing.excerpt: The intention is to avoid the problems current copyright laws create for the sharing of information.

outgoing.name: San Francisco, California
outgoing.excerpt: Headquartered in San Francisco, Creative Commons was officially launched in 2001.

outgoing.name: Wikipedia
outgoing.excerpt: The GFDL was intended mainly as a license for software documentation, but is also in active use by non-software projects such as Wikipedia.
